n2-set-13-q-1.translation: Blanketed by the Pacific High, there are many sunny days and intense heat continues in various regions.
n2-set-13-q-1.correctAnswerEnglish: oowarete / 覆われて - passive form of 覆う, meaning to be covered, veiled, or blanketed.

choices.reason: Oowarete is the correct reading of 覆われて (覆う = おおう, to cover).
Nerawarete is the passive form of 狙う (ねらう, to aim at or target).
Mimawarete is the passive form of 見舞う (みまう, to be struck by a disaster or illness).
Tamerawarete is the passive form of 躊躇う (ためらう, to hesitate).

n2-set-13-q-2.translation: His athletic reflexes are exceptionally outstanding.
n2-set-13-q-2.correctAnswerEnglish: batsugun / 抜群 - preeminent, outstanding, or superlative.

choices.reason: Batsukun incorrectly leaves 群 unvoiced as くん.
Bakkun incorrectly geminates the consonant and unvoices 群.
Batsugun is the correct reading of 抜群 (抜 = ばつ, 群 = ぐん); 抜群にいい means exceptionally good.
Baggun incorrectly geminates the first syllable as ばっ.

n2-set-13-q-3.translation: Looking up at the whale specimen in the museum, I truly realized its immense size.
n2-set-13-q-3.correctAnswerEnglish: hyouhon / 標本 - specimen, sample, or mounted specimen.

choices.reason: Byouhon incorrectly voices 標 as びょう.
Hyoubon incorrectly voices 本 as ぼん.
Hyouhon is the correct reading of 標本 (標 = ひょう, 本 = ほん).
Byoubon incorrectly voices both kanji.

n2-set-13-q-4.translation: Because it is an old personal computer, its operation is sluggish.
n2-set-13-q-4.correctAnswerEnglish: nibui / 鈍い - sluggish, dull, slow, or dim.

choices.reason: Toroi is a colloquial adjective meaning slow or sluggish, but it is not the kanji reading of 鈍い.
Hayai is the reading of 早い or 速い (fast), the opposite of slow.
Warui is the reading of 悪い (bad).
Nibui is the correct reading of 鈍い; 動作が鈍い describes sluggish computer performance or reflexes.

n2-set-13-q-5.translation: Ever since she was a child, she thought about becoming a doctor and contributing to society.
n2-set-13-q-5.correctAnswerEnglish: kouken / 貢献 - contribution; 世の中に貢献する means to contribute to society.

choices.reason: Mitsuken misreads 貢 using its kun-yomi mitsu (from 貢ぐ).
Kouken is the correct reading of 貢献 (貢 = こう, 献 = けん).
Mitsukon incorrectly reads both kanji.
Koukon misreads 献 as こん.

n2-set-13-q-6.translation: People who overestimate themselves are prone to feeling depressed over even minor failures.
n2-set-13-q-6.correctAnswerEnglish: kadai / 過大 - excessive or exaggerated; 過大評価 means overestimation.

choices.reason: 仮大 is a nonexistent compound; 仮 means temporary or provisional.
加大 is an invalid compound; 加 means add or increase.
過大 is the correct kanji (過 = excessive, 大 = great); 過大評価 means overestimating oneself.
課大 is an invalid compound; 課 refers to a lesson or department.

n2-set-13-q-7.translation: He won the championship with a stellar time, shortening the world record by an astonishing 0.5 seconds.
n2-set-13-q-7.correctAnswerEnglish: chijimeru / 縮める - to shorten, reduce, or shrink a record or distance.

choices.reason: 縮める is the correct kanji; 記録を縮める is the standard expression for shaving time off a record.
減める is invalid okurigana for 減 (the verbs are 減らす or 減じる).
損める is a nonexistent word; 損 is used in 損なう (to harm/damage).
短める is an incorrect formation; the standard phrase is 短くする, not 短める.

n2-set-13-q-8.translation: The company president's final decision will never change.
n2-set-13-q-8.correctAnswerEnglish: saishuu / 最終 - final, ultimate, or closing; 最終決定 means final decision.

choices.reason: 再終 is a nonexistent compound combining 再 (again) and 終 (end).
最終 is the correct kanji compound; 最終決定 means final, definitive decision.
再修 means re-studying or repeating a course, not final.
最修 is an invalid compound using 修 (discipline/repair).

n2-set-13-q-9.translation: She shares housework and child-rearing with her husband, continuing to work as a dual-income couple.
n2-set-13-q-9.correctAnswerEnglish: buntan / 分担 - division of labor, sharing, or allotment of duties.

choices.reason: 分拍 is an invalid compound combining 分 with 拍 (beat/clap).
分拒 is an invalid compound combining 分 with 拒 (refuse).
分抽 is an invalid compound combining 分 with 抽 (extract).
分担 is the correct kanji compound (分 = divide, 担 = bear/undertake); 分担する means to share a load or responsibility.

n2-set-13-q-10.translation: Paying taxes is a citizen's duty.
n2-set-13-q-10.correctAnswerEnglish: osameru / 納める - to pay, supply, or deliver fees/taxes; 税金を納める means paying taxes.

choices.reason: 主める is an invalid kanji-okurigana pair.
納める is the correct kanji; 税金を納める specifically means paying taxes to the state.
押める is an invalid combination; 押す means to push.
得める is an invalid combination; 得る is read eru or uru.

n2-set-13-q-11.translation: This hall can be used for multipurpose activities.
n2-set-13-q-11.correctAnswerEnglish: tamokuteki / 多目的 - multipurpose; prefix 多- (ta-) means multi- or numerous.

choices.reason: 多 (ta-) attaches to 目的 to form 多目的, the standard term for multipurpose facilities.
数 (suu-) means several; 数目的 is not an established compound.
複 (fuku-) means compound or plural (e.g. 複数, 複合), but 多目的 is the established word for multipurpose.
高 (kou-) means high; 高目的 is not a valid word.

n2-set-13-q-12.translation: For me, who hails from Hawaii, my first experience seeing snow was in Hokkaido, Japan.
n2-set-13-q-12.correctAnswerEnglish: hatsutaiken / 初体験 - first experience; prefix 初- (hatsu-) indicates the very first time.

choices.reason: 本 (hon-) means main or this, but 本体験 is not a compound.
現 (gen-) means current or actual, but 現体験 is not standard.
初 (hatsu-) attaches to 体験 to form 初体験, meaning one's very first experience of something.
新 (shin-) means new; 新体験 means a novel experience, but the first time in one's life is 初体験.

n2-set-13-q-13.translation: The completion of the new station building is scheduled for the end of the fiscal year.
n2-set-13-q-13.correctAnswerEnglish: nendou matsu / 年度末 - end of the fiscal or academic year; suffix -末 (-matsu) means end.

choices.reason: 次 (-ji) indicates order or sequence; 年度次 is not a compound.
後 (-go) means after; 年度後 is not the standard expression.
期 (-ki) means period or term; 年度期 is redundant and nonstandard.
末 (-matsu) combines with 年度 to form 年度末, meaning the end of the fiscal/school year.

n2-set-13-q-14.translation: The age bracket of that idol group's fans is centered on teenagers.
n2-set-13-q-14.correctAnswerEnglish: nenreisou / 年齢層 - age demographic or age bracket; suffix -層 (-sou) indicates a stratum or group.

choices.reason: 別 (-betsu) means categorized by (e.g. 年齢別), functioning adverbially rather than as a noun subject.
層 (-sou) combines with 年齢 to form 年齢層, the standard sociological term for an age demographic.
間 (-kan) denotes an interval or relation; 年齢間 is not a standard noun.
代 (-dai) denotes an age era or decade (e.g. 10代), but 年齢代 is not a compound.

n2-set-13-q-15.translation: According to the weather forecast, the rain will turn into a steady downpour in the afternoon.
n2-set-13-q-15.correctAnswerEnglish: honburi / 本降り - steady downpour or full-blown rain; prefix 本- (hon-) denotes genuine or full-scale.

choices.reason: 本 (hon-) attaches to 降り to form 本降り (ほんぶり), meaning steady, continuous, full-scale rain.
上 (jou-) means upper; 上降り is not a Japanese word.
少 (shou-) means little; 少降り is not a compound.
総 (sou-) means total or all; 総降り is not a compound.

n2-set-13-q-16.translation: When plants evaporate moisture drawn up through their roots, they absorb heat from their surroundings, which helps combat high temperatures.
n2-set-13-q-16.correctAnswerEnglish: jouhatsu / 蒸発 - evaporation; 水分を蒸発させる means to evaporate moisture.

choices.reason: Haisui refers to drainage or discharging wastewater from pipes.
Sakujo refers to deletion, erasure, or elimination of text/files.
Shouhi means economic consumption or expenditure of resources.
Jouhatsu means evaporation; plants evaporating water cools the surrounding air.

n2-set-13-q-17.translation: When I took the plunge and threw away unused items, the room became clutter-free and felt great.
n2-set-13-q-17.correctAnswerEnglish: sukkiri / すっきり - refreshed, clean, neat, and clutter-free.

choices.reason: Sukkiri describes an environment or feeling becoming light, uncluttered, and orderly.
Hakkiri means clearly, distinctly, or plainly, as in clear visibility or speech.
Sukkari means completely, entirely, or thoroughly (e.g. すっかり忘れた).
Shikkari means firmly, tightly, or reliably (e.g. しっかり掴む).

n2-set-13-q-18.translation: Even though that very wealthy couple is materially satisfied, they are spiritually starved.
n2-set-13-q-18.correctAnswerEnglish: uete / 飢えて - te-form of 飢える, meaning to starve or thirst for emotionally/spiritually.

choices.reason: Warete is from 割れる, meaning to crack, split, or divide.
Morete is from 漏れる, meaning to leak or seep out.
Uete is from 飢える; 精神的に飢えている means spiritually or emotionally starved.
Sorete is from 逸れる, meaning to stray off path or deviate.

n2-set-13-q-19.translation: In the middle of the Egyptian desert, a colossal pyramid towers into the sky.
n2-set-13-q-19.correctAnswerEnglish: kyodai / 巨大 - gigantic, colossal, or enormous in physical size.

choices.reason: Kyoudai (強大) means mighty or powerful, describing military or political force.
Tadai (多大) means tremendous or heavy, describing abstract amounts (e.g. 多大な損害).
Boudai (膨大) means vast or immense in volume or expenditure (e.g. 膨大なデータ).
Kyodai (巨大) describes enormous physical scale, perfectly fitting a towering desert pyramid.

n2-set-13-q-20.translation: Although he is popular in France, in Japan he is still a relatively unknown and niche singer.
n2-set-13-q-20.correctAnswerEnglish: mainaa / マイナー - minor, lesser-known, or non-mainstream.

choices.reason: Hangurii means hungry in the sense of ambitious or fiercely driven.
Popyuraa means popular, which directly contradicts the contrast with フランスでは人気があるが.
Mainaa means minor or niche, contrasting his French fame with his lack of mainstream recognition in Japan.
Furii means free, freelance, or unconstrained.

n2-set-13-q-21.translation: Career guidance is being made mandatory in the educational curricula of universities and junior colleges.
n2-set-13-q-21.correctAnswerEnglish: katei / 課程 - curriculum, course of study; 教育課程 means educational curriculum.

choices.reason: Katei (課程) refers to an academic curriculum or course of instruction (教育課程).
Renshuu means practice, training, or drill.
Katei (過程) means a process, progress, or sequence of events (e.g. 進化の過程).
Katsudou means physical or social activity.

n2-set-13-q-22.translation: What is vital during an earthquake is surviving; as long as the escape route is not cut off, other things will manage somehow.
n2-set-13-q-22.correctAnswerEnglish: dasshutsu / 脱出 - escape, breakout, or evacuation; 脱出経路 means escape route.

choices.reason: Chuudan means suspension or temporary stoppage of an operation.
Dasshutsu means escape; 脱出経路 is the established technical term for an emergency escape/evacuation route.
Deguchi means exit doorway; one says 出口 itself, not 出口経路.
Shutsujou means appearing or participating in an athletic match or event.

n2-set-13-q-23.translation: That athlete has already passed their prime.
n2-set-13-q-23.correctAnswerEnglish: piiku / ピーク - peak, zenith, or prime; 盛り (sakari) means the prime or peak of one's ability.

choices.reason: Rimitto means limit or restriction.
Gooru means goal or finish line.
Piiku means peak; 盛りを過ぎた accurately equates to being past one's athletic peak (ピークを過ぎた).
Chekkupointo means checkpoint or inspection station.

n2-set-13-q-24.translation: The effectiveness of educational pedigree when seeking employment still retains some potency.
n2-set-13-q-24.correctAnswerEnglish: kouryoku / 効力 - efficacy, validity, or effective power; 有効性 means validity or effectiveness.

choices.reason: Kouryoku means effectiveness or validity, closely matching 有効性.
Imi means meaning or significance.
Hyouka means evaluation, appraisal, or rating.
Sontoku means advantage and disadvantage, or profit and loss.

n2-set-13-q-25.translation: Academic achievement tests for elementary school students were conducted all at once nationwide.
n2-set-13-q-25.correctAnswerEnglish: douji ni / 同時に - simultaneously or all at the same time; いっせいに means all at once.

choices.reason: Betsubetsu ni means separately or individually.
Zokuzoku to means continuously or one after another in succession.
Douji ni means simultaneously, accurately paraphrasing 全国でいっせいに (all across the country at the same time).
Totsuzen ni means suddenly or unexpectedly.

n2-set-13-q-26.translation: The mother senses and sees through her son's inner feelings.
n2-set-13-q-26.correctAnswerEnglish: minuite / 見抜いて - seeing through or discerning; 察する means to perceive or read unspoken thoughts.

choices.reason: Yosoku shite means predicting or forecasting future developments.
Minuite means seeing through to the underlying reality, accurately matching 気持ちを察している.
Ukettote means receiving or taking in information.
Sonchou shite means respecting or honoring someone's stance.

n2-set-13-q-27.translation: To leak confidential company information to outsiders.
n2-set-13-q-27.correctAnswerEnglish: kougai suru / 口外する - to disclose, tell outsiders, or let slip; リークする means to leak information.

choices.reason: Kougai suru means disclosing or speaking of confidential matters to outsiders, matching リークする.
Riyou suru means utilizing or taking advantage of something.
Seigen suru means restricting or limiting access.
Konran saseru means throwing into chaos or causing confusion.

n2-set-13-q-28.translation: Tests are conducted in order to measure children's athletic ability.
n2-set-13-q-28.correctAnswerEnglish: sokutei / 測定 - measurement or gauging; 運動能力を測定する means to measure physical/athletic performance.

choices.reason: Investigating the cause of an accident should use 調査している (investigating), not 測定.
Anticipating minor troubles in advance should use 予測していた (anticipated), not 測定していた.
Forecasting an earthquake in a region should use 予測した or 推定した, not 測定した.
運動能力を測定する is the precise standard term for testing and measuring athletic or physical capabilities.

n2-set-13-q-29.translation: What that guy says is completely irrational and lacks all logical coherence.
n2-set-13-q-29.correctAnswerEnglish: suji / 筋 - logic, coherent thread, or reason; 筋が通る means to make sense logically.

choices.reason: Innate musical pitch is described as 才能 (talent) or 素質 (aptitude), not 筋.
筋が通っていない is the established idiom meaning lacking logical sense or coherence.
Clashing constantly with a boss in temperament should use 馬が合わない or 意見が合わない, not 筋が合わない.
Incomprehensible behavior reflects strange 動機 (motive) or 意図 (intent), not 筋.

n2-set-13-q-30.translation: If it's him, he would certainly never do something cowardly and dishonest like running away halfway through.
n2-set-13-q-30.correctAnswerEnglish: hikyou / ひきょう - cowardly, unfair, foul, or sneaky.

choices.reason: 途中で逃げ出すようなひきょうなこと describes running away from responsibility, which is genuinely cowardly and unfair.
An undesirable TV program for children should be called 下品な (vulgar) or くだらない (worthless), not ひきょうな.
Applying makeup on a public train is considered マナーが悪い (bad manners) or はしたない (improper), not ひきょう.
A disgraceful drunken appearance seen by a girlfriend is called みっともない or 無様な, not ひきょうな.

n2-set-13-q-31.translation: Regarding this issue, there is a large divergence of views between the elderly and the young.
n2-set-13-q-31.correctAnswerEnglish: kenkai / 見解 - opinion, outlook, view, or perspective on an issue; 見解の差 means difference of views.

choices.reason: Asking for helpful input or suggestions should use いいアイデア or いい意見, not いい見解.
Expressions of dissatisfaction raised across the board should be 不満の声 (voices of dissatisfaction), not 不満の見解.
Expressing one's formal resolve to work harder should use 努力をする所存 (intention/resolve), not 見解.
見解の差 is the established phrase for differences in viewpoints or philosophical stances between groups.

n2-set-13-q-32.translation: I checked the errors in my essay, made a clean fair copy, and submitted it.
n2-set-13-q-32.correctAnswerEnglish: seisho / 清書 - making a fair copy, writing out a clean final draft without errors.

choices.reason: Government annual reports are called 白書 (white paper) or 報告書, not 清書.
Quickly jotting down a phone number on a scrap of paper is called メモして, not 清書して.
清書して出した correctly describes rewriting a corrected rough draft into a neat, error-free final submission.
Filling in one's name and address at a reception desk is called ご記入ください, not 清書してください.

n2-set-13-q-33.translation: Training for rookie firefighters is carried out strictly, spanning as long as half a year.
n2-set-13-q-33.correctAnswerEnglish: watatte / 渡って - spanning or extending over; 〜に（も）わたって denotes extent across time or space.

choices.reason: Kakatte would express time taken (半年もかかって), but cannot follow the particle に as 半年にもかかって.
Watatte (半年にも渡って) correctly expresses a continuous process extending across the span of six months.
Tsuzuite means continuing and does not pair with にも in this manner.
Sugite means exceeding or passing beyond (半年を過ぎて), which does not fit here.

n2-set-13-q-34.translation: Anyone who has information regarding the perpetrator, please inform your nearest police station.
n2-set-13-q-34.correctAnswerEnglish: ni kansuru / に関する - regarding or concerning; marks the topic of information.

choices.reason: Ni oyobu means extending or reaching up to a substantial figure or scope.
Ni tomonau means accompanying or occurring alongside another event.
Ni sou means in line with or following a plan or guidelines.
Ni kansuru (犯人に関する情報) is the standard adnominal phrase for information regarding the suspect.

n2-set-13-q-35.translation: Just when you thought the baby was crying a moment ago, it is already smiling brightly.
n2-set-13-q-35.correctAnswerEnglish: naite ita ka / 泣いていたか - was crying; 〜たかと思ったら expresses an immediate, astonishing transition.

choices.reason: Naite ita ka combines with と思ったら to form 泣いていたかと思ったら, expressing a rapid shift from tears to smiles.
Nakou ka would form 泣こうか泣くまいか (wondering whether to cry), which does not fit.
Nakanai ka means wondering if it won't cry.
Nakumai ka expresses an intention not to cry, which does not fit a baby's rapid mood change.

n2-set-13-q-36.translation: After keeping us waiting endlessly, what that restaurant served in the end was completely different from what was on the menu.
n2-set-13-q-36.correctAnswerEnglish: ageku / あげく - in the end / after all that; 〜たあげく indicates an undesirable outcome after a long ordeal.

choices.reason: Sei ka means perhaps because of, which does not link an extensive ordeal to an ultimate letdown.
Tokoro simply marks a temporal occasion upon doing something, lacking the negative culmination nuance.
Ageku (待たせたあげく) specifically denotes an exasperating or negative final result after a prolonged process.
Dokoroka means far from or let alone, expressing contrastive degree.

n2-set-13-q-37.translation: Customs that are completely natural from the perspective of Japanese people are often strange when seen from other countries.
n2-set-13-q-37.correctAnswerEnglish: ni shitara / にしたら - from the viewpoint / perspective of; indicates someone's standpoint.

choices.reason: Ni shitemo means even if or even for, expressing concessive allowance rather than perspective.
Ni shitara (日本人にしたらい) means from the standpoint or viewpoint of Japanese people.
Ni oitemo means also in or also at a location/field.
Ni oite means in or at a location or occasion.

n2-set-13-q-38.translation: For the fatigue accompanying computer work, exercising is better rather than simply resting.
n2-set-13-q-38.correctAnswerEnglish: tomonau / 伴う - accompanying or going hand in hand with; 〜に伴う describes an associated consequence.

choices.reason: Motodzuku means based upon (e.g. 事実に基づく).
Oyobosu is a transitive verb meaning to exert an effect (e.g. 影響を及ぼす).
Tomonau (作業に伴う疲れ) correctly describes fatigue that naturally accompanies or arises from computer work.
Tsuujiru means leading to, passing through, or being understood.

n2-set-13-q-39.translation: There is no way that someone like me, who is merely an ordinary salaried worker, could buy such a massive house.
n2-set-13-q-39.correctAnswerEnglish: suginai / 過ぎない - nothing more than / merely; 〜に過ぎない indicates an action or status is merely that and nothing more.

choices.reason: Kawaranai means no different from.
Naranai means does not become, or expresses obligation in 〜てはならない.
Oyobanai means does not reach or cannot match.
Suginai forms に過ぎない, humbly emphasizing that the speaker is merely an ordinary worker.

n2-set-13-q-40.translation: Taking four hours, the runner ran the full 42.195 kilometers to the very finish.
n2-set-13-q-40.correctAnswerEnglish: nuita / ぬいた - pushed through to the end; 動詞ます形＋ぬく means doing an exhausting task completely to the finish.

choices.reason: Kaketa indicates starting an action or being in the middle of it, not completing it.
Nuita (走りぬいた) expresses persevering through hardship to complete the entire marathon distance.
Tootta means passed through; Japanese uses 走り通した, not 走り通った.
Satta means ran away or departed.

n2-set-13-q-41.translation: I am terribly sorry to trouble you, but could you please send the documents urgently? They are needed for tomorrow's meeting.
n2-set-13-q-41.correctAnswerEnglish: okutte itadakenai deshou ka / 送っていただけないでしょうか - could you please send; polite request asking a favor.

choices.reason: Okutte itadaketa deshou ka is an unnatural past phrasing when requesting a future action.
Okutte itadakenai deshou ka is the standard humble, highly polite request for asking someone to send documents.
Okureba yoroshii deshou ka asks if the speaker should send them, reversing the requested actor.
Okutte yoroshii deshou ka asks for permission for the speaker to send something.

n2-set-13-q-42.translation: The umbrellas placed at this station are permitted to be borrowed freely according to policy, but please be sure to return them.
n2-set-13-q-42.correctAnswerEnglish: yoi koto ni natte iru / よいことになっている - it is the established rule/arrangement that it is allowed.

choices.reason: Yoi koto ni natte iru indicates an established regulation or custom that allows commuters to borrow umbrellas.
Yoi hazu wa nai means there is no way it is permissible, which contradicts the station's service.
Yoi koto ni mo natte iru adds an awkward particle も that disrupts the clear policy statement.
Yokunai hazu wa nai is a convoluted double negative inappropriate for simple permission.

n2-set-13-q-43.translation: At a time like this when a typhoon is approaching, one should definitely not go out to sea.
n2-set-13-q-43.correctAnswerEnglish: deru beki de wa nai / 出るべきではない - should not go out; 〜べきではない states a firm moral/common-sense prohibition.

choices.reason: Deru yori hokawai means has no choice but to go out, which is dangerously irresponsible in a typhoon.
Denai beki da is grammatically nonstandard; Japanese expresses negative obligation as 出るべきではない.
Deru beki de wa nai expresses the authoritative common-sense judgment that going out to sea is strictly prohibited.
Denai wake ni wa ikanai means cannot avoid going out, which is the exact opposite of safety wisdom.

n2-set-13-q-44.translation: I knew it from photographs, but the real Mount Fuji is a mountain so beautiful that the more you gaze at it, the more beautiful it seems.
n2-set-13-q-44.correctAnswerEnglish: mireba miru hodo / 見れば見るほど - the more you look, the more...; 〜ば〜ほど expresses escalating degree.

choices.reason: Mitara miru hodo mixes たら and ほど, which is nonstandard grammar for this correlative pattern.
Mitemo miru to is an ungrammatical combination.
Mireba miru hodo (見れば見るほど) is the established N2 structure expressing that appreciation increases the more one looks.
Miyou to mimai to means whether you look at it or not.

n2-set-13-q-45.translation: Among books aimed at children, there are many that are also interesting for adults.
n2-set-13-q-45.correctAnswerEnglish: hon no naka ni wa / 本の中には - among books; the star is option 2 in 子ども向けの本の中には大人にとって.

choices.reason: Otona ni pairs with とって in the third position to form 大人にとって.
Hon no naka ni wa fills the second blank at the star, defining the category of books aimed at kids.
Totte completes 大人にとって before おもしろい, occupying the fourth position.
Muke no attaches to 子ども to form 子ども向けの, occupying the first position.

n2-set-13-q-46.translation: At that restaurant, the prices are cheap and the food is delicious, but the trouble is that it is always crowded.
n2-set-13-q-46.correctAnswerEnglish: yasukereba / 安ければ - if cheap; the star is option 4 in 値段も安ければ味もよい.

choices.reason: Nedan mo begins the parallel comparison with price, occupying the first position.
Aji mo follows 安ければ in the third position to introduce the quality of taste.
Yoi completes the parallel phrase 味もよい before が, in the fourth position.
Yasukereba pairs with 値段も to form 値段も安ければ, filling the second blank at the star.

n2-set-13-q-47.translation: With the former president's son as the new president, we will launch a new organizational structure.
n2-set-13-q-47.correctAnswerEnglish: to shite / として - as; the star is option 3 in 新社長として新しい体制.

choices.reason: Atarashii pre-modifies 体制, occupying the third position after the star.
Shin-shachou identifies the new role, occupying the first position.
To shite marks the new role (新社長として), filling the second blank at the star.
Taisei is the direct object noun before をスタートさせる, occupying the fourth position.

n2-set-13-q-48.translation: Leaving aside soy sauce, Japanese cuisine cannot even be spoken of.
n2-set-13-q-48.correctAnswerEnglish: nihon ryouri / 日本料理 - Japanese cuisine; the star is option 1 in ぬきにしては日本料理は語れない.

choices.reason: Nihon ryouri serves as the subject noun and fills the second blank at the star.
Wa is the topic particle following 日本料理 in the third position.
Nuki ni shite wa follows しょうゆを in the first position to express 'leaving aside / without'.
Katarenai is the potential negative predicate meaning 'cannot be discussed', occupying the fourth position.

n2-set-13-q-49.translation: Upon learning that their daughter was safe, the family was in an uproar, crying and laughing all at once.
n2-set-13-q-49.correctAnswerEnglish: warau / 笑う - to laugh; the star is option 2 in 泣くやら笑うやらで.

choices.reason: Wakatte connects the news of safety with the outburst of emotions, occupying the first position.
Warau pairs with やらで in 泣くやら笑うやらで, filling the third blank at the star.
Naku yara begins the alternating emotional expressions in the second position.
Yara de concludes the compound emotion pattern before 家族は大騒ぎだった, in the fourth position.

n2-set-13-q-50.translation: The left brain is responsible for words and logic, while the right brain is responsible for sensory inputs such as shapes and sounds. Therefore, in order to enhance thinking ability, it is necessary to train both.
n2-set-13-q-50.correctAnswerEnglish: shitagatte / したがって - therefore, accordingly, consequently; option 1 logically introduces the conclusion.

choices.reason: Shitagatte logically draws the rational consequence from the preceding sentence that both brain hemispheres must be cultivated.
To wa ie means nevertheless, which would contrast with rather than conclude from the premise.
Aruiwa means or / alternatively, which presents choices rather than a deductive conclusion.
Shikamo means moreover, which merely adds supplementary detail rather than a logical inference.

n2-set-13-q-51.translation: It is said that Plato, the great philosopher of ancient Greece, gave lectures to his disciples while walking.
n2-set-13-q-51.correctAnswerEnglish: arukinagara kougi shita / 歩きながら講義した - lectured while walking; option 1 expresses simultaneous actions.

choices.reason: Arukinagara kougi shita accurately expresses continuous simultaneous action (lecturing while walking), matching historical accounts.
Aruita mama denotes leaving a completed physical state unchanged, which does not fit ongoing locomotion.
Aruku sai ni denotes on the formal occasion of walking, rather than an uninterrupted activity during a walk.
Aruku tsuide ni would diminish lecturing to a trivial secondary errand done while walking.

n2-set-13-q-52.translation: When producing ideas through verbal debate, the logical left brain becomes active, but the right brain tends to become idle.
n2-set-13-q-52.correctAnswerEnglish: yasumi-gachi ni narimasu / 休みがちになります - tends to rest / become inactive; option 3 contrasts with 活発になります.

choices.reason: Kappatsu ni narimasu (becomes active) directly contradicts the grammatical contrast introduced by が.
Ikii-to shimasu (becomes lively) also contradicts the opposition between the two hemispheres.
Yasumi-gachi ni narimasu uses 〜がち to express the recurring negative tendency of the right brain to become understimulated.
Yasumi-sou ni narimasu suggests it looks as though it is about to rest, which does not describe an ongoing state.

n2-set-13-q-53.translation: As a result, even if an idea does come to mind, it often ends up being rejected as 'unrealistic.'
n2-set-13-q-53.correctAnswerEnglish: hitei sareru / 否定される - to be denied, rejected, or dismissed; option 4 matches 「現実的でない」.

choices.reason: Sansei sareru means to be agreed with or endorsed, opposite to the criticism 'not realistic.'
Koutei sareru means to be affirmed or validated, which contradicts the harsh dismissal.
Hansei sareru means to be reflected upon with regret, which does not describe appraising an idea.
Hitei sareru means to be rejected or dismissed, perfectly matching the skeptical judgment that an idea is unrealistic.

n2-set-13-q-54.translation: When you begin concentrating on walking, left-brain thinking weakens, and the sensory right brain enters a state where it can easily function.
n2-set-13-q-54.correctAnswerEnglish: a sanou / b unou - left brain / right brain; option 3 correctly pairs verbal logic with the left brain and sensory ideas with the right brain.

choices.reason: Assigning both a and b to the left brain is nonsensical and ignores the hemispheric contrast.
Assigning both a and b to the right brain also contradicts the dual-hemisphere model.
Assigning a to the left brain (logical thinking weakens) and b to the right brain (sensory ideation activates) matches the entire thesis.
Inverting the roles by assigning a to the right brain and b to the left brain contradicts the brain definitions established in the passage.
